steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Latin prose style analyses HOW an author writes, not just WHAT they say. Style includes word order, sentence length, rhythm, and rhetorical devices. | Key Fact: Word order in Latin is flexible and significant: placing a word first or last gives it emphasis. The first and last positions in a sentence are the most emphatic. | Key Fact: Hyperbaton is the separation of an adjective from its noun, which draws attention to both words and creates a literary effect (e.g. 'magna cum virtute' rather than 'cum magna virtute'). | Key Fact: Reported speech (oratio obliqua) allows authors to present events through characters' perspectives, creating drama and showing different viewpoints without direct speech.
